next_step: Closed-lost to hyperscaler managed endpoint. Capture notes, update playbook, follow-up EOM+6 months.
timeline: 2024-04-02: Incoming lead from partner integration event — initial qualification by AE (Samir)
2024-04-09: Discovery call — use-case: multi-tenant chat + semantic search; high throughput for support chat; latency target <200ms P95
2024-05-07: Technical deep-dive with SE (Renee) — validated latency on dedicated pool, demo of KV cache, batching trade-offs
2024-06-03: Security questionnaire submitted; asked for SOC2 + KMS integration details
2024-06-21: Stakeholder call with CTO (Fireflies id ff_20240621_verdigris_eval) — CTO mentions preference to consolidate on single hyperscaler
2024-07-10: Pricing review — procurement requests TCO comparison vs AWS managed endpoints
2024-07-25: POC period started (2 weeks) — Redwood dedicated vs customer-managed SageMaker endpoints
2024-08-06: POC wrap; evaluation team preferred hyperscaler due to existing discounts, consolidated billing, and internal policy
2024-08-12: Final procurement meeting — decision to select AWS managed endpoints; Redwood marked closed-lost
2024-08-29: AE updated record, set follow-up cadence and captured lessons learned
notes: Key pain: reduce token cost while keeping sub-200ms P95 for chat. Strong need for prefix caching and deterministic fallbacks.
CTO quote (6/21): "We'd prefer to keep everything in AWS — one vendor, one bill. If pricing gap closes, we'll revisit."
Procurement rationale: consolidated contract with cloud provider, existing enterprise discount with AWS, internal mandate to use cloud-native managed endpoints where possible.
Security review found no hard-blockers for Redwood but legal wants single-vendor data flow diagram for audit — procurement saw this as more work vs native service.
SE notes: Redwood performance met latency targets in lab; cost per concurrent user higher for Redwood dedicated in initial config vs SageMaker multi-node with credits.
Customer POC notes: observed marginally lower tail latency on their in-cloud managed endpoints; they valued ease of IAM integration and existing infra automation.
"Next steps" owned by AE: close-lost updated, send win/loss summary to Sales Ops, extract pricing delta, add recommended mitigations to playbook.
Internal ask: document a short rebuttal pack for future hyperscaler consolidation objections (migration guides, KMS flow, cost delta examples).
Follow-up plan: re-engage at 6 months or if internal cloud mandate changes; provide updated Optimize recommendations if they reopen.
